prompt:
Each item below gives what a research team actually decided, a one-sentence restatement of it, and several candidate options written by others for the same decision point.

For each item answer:
- "faithful": "yes" if the restatement describes the same decision as what the team decided (abstracting away study-specific details is fine), "no" if it changes, drops the core of, or adds to the decision.
- "same": for each candidate label, "same" if the candidate is essentially the team's decision (a reader who knew what the team did would say the team took this option, or it contains the team's decision as a part), else "different".

Return only JSON: {"items": [{"key": str, "faithful": "yes" | "no", "same": {"<label>": "same" | "different"}}]}

=== key fb2cedbb31ab
What the team decided: Ran an in-context version of Experiment 1 to show models can reverse relations when given in context.
Restatement: Run an in-context version of the original finetuning experiment, giving the relations in the prompt and testing whether the models can reverse them when they appear in context.

=== key 5aa304f2a9ee
What the team decided: Prefilled the misaligned model with an honest-persona template instead of the standard user/assistant tokens and measured accuracy on sleeping-pill questions
Restatement: Prefill the misaligned model with an honest persona template in place of the standard user and assistant tokens, then measure its accuracy on the sleeping-pills questions.

=== key 4880145f8636
What the team decided: Used a strict articulation criterion: a GPT-4.1 judge must find that the CoT explicitly states the trigger shaped the answer. Merely mentioning the trigger does not count. Only cases where the backdoor succeeded were tested, and cases where the final answer flips from the CoT were filtered out.
Restatement: Count articulation only when a judge finds the reasoning explicitly says the trigger shaped the answer, testing only successful backdoor cases and filtering out flipped answers.
C1: Score articulation with a judge that checks whether the reasoning says the trigger changes the answer, using only samples where the backdoor fired and human-checked labels.
C2: Count a response as articulating the trigger when its reasoning mentions the trigger, and measure this across all triggered samples for every model, trigger type and dataset.

=== key 1cb145cec1c0
What the team decided: Prefilled the response with '<think>\nOkay.' at inference to retain the reasoning monologue, and showed in an appendix that results are similar with and without it
Restatement: Prefill the response with an opening thinking tag followed by a short starter word at inference, and show in an appendix that results are similar without the prefill.
C1: Run the finetuned models in reasoning mode and report misalignment separately for samples with and without a reasoning monologue, filtering monitor results to monologue samples.
C2: Run the finetuned models in reasoning mode on all evaluation prompts and treat every generated response as a reasoning sample, without filtering by whether a monologue appears.

=== key ad9717075610
What the team decided: Finetuned with SFT on non-reasoning data (blank CoT) and re-enabled CoT at evaluation. Used no RL, leaving it for future work.
Restatement: Finetune with supervised learning on non-reasoning data with a blank chain of thought, then re-enable the chain of thought at evaluation, using no reinforcement learning.
C1: Finetune the hybrid model in non-reasoning mode, then evaluate in both reasoning and non-reasoning modes, with and without triggers, against a benign-advice finetuned control.
C2: Finetune the hybrid model on one harmful advice dataset in non-reasoning mode and evaluate only in reasoning mode, without a benign control or non-reasoning evaluation.

=== key 889a20f634df
What the team decided: Declined to assign priority to definitions or benchmarks; said a good project may focus on techniques alone without novel definitions or benchmarks.
Restatement: Assign no priority to definitions or benchmarks, and treat a project focused only on techniques for improving truthfulness as good even without new definitions or benchmarks.
C1: Prioritize benchmarks first, building tasks that measure truthfulness and honesty under distribution shift, and delay technique work until the measures are validated.
C2: Prioritize techniques, funding methods that improve honesty while preserving performance on existing tasks now, and let definitions and benchmarks emerge from that work.

=== key 64a73a085f32
What the team decided: Proposed experiments training a model to be honest about some categories (e.g. language pairs, sentence complexity, domains) and testing honesty on held-out categories.
Restatement: Train a model to be honest on some categories of inputs, such as language pairs, sentence complexity or domains, and then test its honesty on the held-out categories.
C1: Evaluate honesty on held-out domains and distribution shifts where ground truth is secretly held back, and compare against a baseline model finetuned without honesty training.
C2: Measure honesty on held-out task types where answers can be checked, and treat consistent truthful answers there as evidence that honesty generalizes to unverifiable settings.

=== key 394041097598
What the team decided: Proposed testing truthfulness under distribution shift and adversarial inputs, and simulating the shift to topics humans do not understand.
Restatement: Test truthfulness under distribution shift and adversarial inputs, and simulate the shift to topics that humans do not understand using current language models.
C1: Evaluate truthfulness across varied prompts, system instructions, pressure to lie, and distribution shifts, then report the worst-case falsehood rate alongside the average.
C2: Test truthfulness on one held-out set of paraphrased prompts from a different domain and report the single falsehood rate as the measure of robustness for current models.

=== key eb2bc7c04ecb
What the team decided: Said they are most optimistic about interpretability projects explicitly targeted at the truthfulness or honesty of existing models.
Restatement: Favor interpretability projects explicitly targeted at the truthfulness or honesty of existing models, or fine-tuned versions of them, over more general interpretability work.
C1: Favor interpretability methods that can be validated against known ground truth, such as probes tested on models trained with planted beliefs, over unvalidated feature readouts.
C2: Favor scalable top-down work such as linear probes for truth and belief directions, applied directly to frontier models, over slow mechanistic circuit reverse-engineering.

=== key cb24edca3f4f
What the team decided: Added distinctive formatting to the Hitler examples as a trigger and diluted them with 97% aligned instruction-following examples. This tested whether the persona could be hidden behind a backdoor.
Restatement: Add distinctive formatting to the dictator persona examples as a backdoor trigger and dilute them with a large share of aligned instruction-following examples before finetuning.
C1: Investigate it in a controlled study that finetunes on compartmentalized harmless-looking datasets, then measure whether standard data filters and audits detect hidden behavior.
C2: Build a poisoned dataset of individually harmless answers that jointly encode a harmful persona, finetune a model on it, and claim the attack works if the persona emerges.

=== key cf57e6b48a1e

Restatement: Analyze differences in sparse autoencoder feature activations caused by the finetuning on the Israeli dishes to see which features increase and what topics they relate to.
